a_records.quote: Now, we present an example to demonstrate that if the smallest order statistics satisfy the conditions of Theorem 4.3, then the survival function of one will be smaller than the other. Example 4.4. Let U_i ∼ q − W(q, λ_i, β) and V_i ∼ q − W(q, λ∗_i, β) for i = 1, 2 be two sets of components being mutually dependent. For the case of 0 < q < 1, we have used Clayton copula with generators ψ_1(u) = 1/(1−u) and ψ_2(u) = 1/√(2u+1) to model the dependence. With the choice of these generators, it is easy to check that the conditions of Theorem 4.3 hold. Figure 9(a) demonstrates that F̄_{U_{1:n}} − F̄_{V_{1:n}} ≤ 0 on (0, D) = (0, 1.384) where λ_1 = 0.5, λ_2 = 1.7, λ★_1 = 0.6, λ★_2 = 1.5, β = 0.5, and q = 0.5. For the case of 1 < q < 2, to model the dependence, we employ the Gumbel-Hougaard copula (member of Archimedean copula family) with generators ψ_1(u) = e^{1−(1+u)^8} and ψ_2(u) = e^{1−(1+u)^3}. Then ϕ_1(u) = (1 − ln u)^{1/8} − 1 and ϕ_2(u) = (1 − ln u)^{1/3} − 1. Observe that both ψ_1(u) and ψ_2(u) are log-concave and ϕ_2◦ψ_1 is super-additive. With the parameter choices λ_1 = 0.5, λ_2 = 0.8, λ★_1 = 0.3, λ★_2 = 0.9, β = 0.5, and q = 1.5, Figure 9(b) demonstrates that the result also holds for 1 < q < 2.

b_records.quote: Now, we present an example to demonstrate that if the smallest order statistics satisfy the conditions of Theorem 4.3, then the survival function of one will be smaller than the other. Example 4.4. Let U_i ∼ q − W(q, λ_i, β) and V_i ∼ q − W(q, λ*_i, β) for i = 1, 2 be two sets of components being mutually dependent. For the case of 1 < q < 2, to model the dependence, we employ the Gumbel-Hougaard copula (member of Archimedean copula family) with generators ψ_1(u) = e^{1−(1+u)^8} and ψ_2(u) = e^{1−(1+u)^3}. Then φ_1(u) = (1 − ln u)^{1/8} − 1 and φ_2(u) = (1 − ln u)^{1/3} − 1. Observe that both ψ_1(u) and ψ_2(u) are log-concave and φ_2∘ψ_1 is super-additive. With the parameter choices λ_1 = 0.5, λ_2 = 0.8, λ*_1 = 0.3, λ*_2 = 0.9, β = 0.5, and q = 1.5, Figure 9(b) demonstrates that the result also holds for 1 < q < 2.
